purpose: Content-address the minimum public first-party facts used by the three-domain functional mapping without copying source prose.

facts: Anthropic describes Opus 5.5 as having strong cybersecurity capability.
Anthropic states routine software-development use includes identifying and fixing bugs in user code.
Anthropic states most cybersecurity tasks are rerouted under production safeguards, with a verification program for trusted cyber practitioners.
Anthropic reports biology capability including long-horizon molecular prediction and design.
Anthropic reports expert assessment of scientific novelty and trusted-access biology R&D.
Anthropic reports automated AI R&D capability for Opus 5.5 at or slightly above its prior frontier comparison, while below its substitution threshold.
Anthropic reports an internal real-engineering test score of 55.8% for Opus 5.5 versus an 85% research-staff substitution reference threshold.
Anthropic lists Opus 5.5 modalities including text, image input, conversation, analysis, coding, creative tasks, text-based artifacts, and diagrams.
Anthropic describes a frozen AI R&D work tree built from roughly 15000 granular internal tasks.
The reported tree has 542 nodes and 378 leaves.
Published leaf examples include evaluation-platform defect diagnosis and fixes, RL sandbox egress and network policy, and serving-incident postmortems.
Anthropic describes AI R&D work as research and engineering performed by agents with varying degrees of human supervision.
